CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hypoxaemia, 2 day(s).

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
A 62-year-old man presenting with hypoxaemia, fever, severe dyspnoea. Symptoms have progressed over 2 day(s). Assessed in the emergency department and admitted for further management and stabilisation. Working diagnosis: ARDS - Post Viral Pneumonia.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, diagnosed 4 years ago after presentation with palpitations and exertional dyspnoea. CHA2DS2-VASc score 2. Anticoagulated with apixaban 5 mg twice daily. Rate control achieved with metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, with resting heart rates of 68-78 bpm in clinic. Electrical cardioversion in March 2025 restored sinus rhythm transiently but atrial fibrillation recurred within 72 hours. Cardiology opted for a rate-control strategy given the patient's age and symptom burden. Echocardiography on 2025-10-30 showed a mildly dilated left atrium at 4.7 cm with an ejection fraction of 58% and no thrombus on transoesophageal imaging. Anticoagulation has been well tolerated with no bleeding episodes. Renal function and full blood count were last checked on 2026-01-21 and were acceptable.

MEDICATIONS ON ADMISSION
1. Apixaban 5 mg PO twice daily
2. Metoprolol succinate 50 mg PO daily
3. Atorvastatin 40 mg PO at night

ALLERGIES
Iodinated contrast (urticaria)

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives with adult child. Semi-retired. Fifteen pack-year smoking history, currently smoking. Denies alcohol or drug use.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Acutely unwell and diaphoretic.
Vital signs: temperature 38.6 C, heart rate 139 bpm, blood pressure 90/47 mmHg, respiratory rate 25, oxygen saturation 84% on 6 L/min nasal cannula. GCS 9.
Focused findings: Diffuse bilateral crackles. Accessory muscle use. Poor chest expansion. No peripheral oedema.

LABORATORY DATA
WBC 25.8 x10^9/L, Hb 7.9 g/dL, platelets 116 x10^9/L, sodium 129 mmol/L, potassium 3.9 mmol/L, creatinine 2.8 mg/dL, lactate 7.5 mmol/L, procalcitonin 21.8 ng/mL, CRP 155 mg/L

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Lung-protective ventilation: Vt 6 mL/kg PBW, plateau pressure <30 cmH2O
2. Prone positioning 16h/day while P/F ratio <150
3. Conservative fluid strategy; daily weights
4. Daily sedation interruption and spontaneous breathing trial assessment
5. Serial ABG q6h and CXR daily
6. Atrial Fibrillation: continue home therapy with dose adjustment guided by current renal and hepatic function; specialty input requested.
7. VTE prophylaxis: enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneously daily.
8. Code status: full, confirmed on admission.

SUBJECTIVE
Patient reports symptoms broadly unchanged. Slept intermittently. Pain score 7/10.

OBJECTIVE
Vital signs: temperature 39.8 C, heart rate 125 bpm, blood pressure 92/57 mmHg, respiratory rate 36, oxygen saturation 83% on BiPAP 12/5. GCS 12.
Fluid balance (24h): 815 mL in, 1019 mL out, net -204 mL.
Focused examination: Diffuse bilateral crackles. Accessory muscle use. Poor chest expansion. No peripheral oedema.

LABORATORY DATA (06:00)
WBC 12.7 x10^9/L, Hb 8.5 g/dL, platelets 132 x10^9/L, sodium 141 mmol/L, potassium 4.7 mmol/L, creatinine 3.4 mg/dL, lactate 7.3 mmol/L, procalcitonin 42.5 ng/mL, CRP 162 mg/L

Convulsions, 4 day(s).

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
A 25-year-old man presenting with convulsions, impaired consciousness, rigors. Symptoms have progressed over 4 day(s). Assessed in the emergency department and admitted for further management and stabilisation. Working diagnosis: Suspected Cerebral Malaria.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, emphysema-predominant, of 15 years' duration. Former smoker with a forty pack-year history. FEV1 65% predicted on most recent spirometry. Currently on triple inhaled therapy. Chronic hypoxaemia managed with home oxygen at 2 L/min continuously, following demonstrated desaturation to 84% on a six-minute walk test without supplementation. MEDICATIONS ON ADMISSION
1. Fluticasone/umeclidinium/vilanterol inhaled daily
2. Albuterol 90 mcg inhaled as required
3. Home oxygen 2 L/min continuous

CHIEF COMPLAINT
Weakness, 2 day(s).

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
A 53-year-old woman presenting with weakness, muscle pain, oliguria. Symptoms have progressed over 2 day(s). Assessed in the emergency department and admitted for further management and stabilisation. Working diagnosis: Acute Kidney Injury - Rhabdomyolysis.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
HIV-1 infection diagnosed 12 years ago. Nadir CD4 count 174 cells/uL. Current antiretroviral therapy is a single-tablet bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide regimen, taken for 5 years. Most recent laboratory results on 2026-02-04 showed a CD4 count of 876 cells/uL with an undetectable viral load below 20 copies/mL, maintained continuously for 3 years. There have been no opportunistic infections. Annual screening has been negative for tuberculosis, with a normal metabolic panel and a lipid profile at target on statin therapy. Hepatitis B surface antibody is positive from vaccination and hepatitis C antibody is negative. Bone densitometry on 2024-05-07 showed a lumbar spine T-score of -1.2, consistent with osteopenia, and calcium with vitamin D supplementation was commenced. Adherence is excellent, supported by pharmacy auto-refill, with six-monthly infectious diseases review.

MEDICATIONS ON ADMISSION
1. Bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide, one tablet PO daily
2. Atorvastatin 10 mg PO at night
3. Calcium 600 mg with vitamin D 400 IU PO daily

ALLERGIES
Codeine (gastrointestinal upset)

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives with adult child. Semi-retired. Fifteen pack-year smoking history, currently smoking. Denies alcohol or drug use.

Vital signs: temperature 39.4 C, heart rate 105 bpm, blood pressure 82/60 mmHg, respiratory rate 30, oxygen saturation 92% on 6 L/min nasal cannula. GCS 12.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Aggressive isotonic crystalloid targeting urine output 200-300 mL/h
2. Serial CK, potassium, phosphate, and calcium q4h

4. Avoid all nephrotoxins including NSAIDs and contrast
5. Cardiac monitoring for hyperkalaemia-related arrhythmia
